s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear
key_facts: Patient has a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy
Patient has chronic kidney disease
Patient presented with altered mental status after an unwitnessed fall
New lesions developed on nose, ear, and arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia
Laboratory tests showed acute kidney injury
Peripheral blood smear showed Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate
Serum and urine protein electrophoreses showed abnormal paraprotein band
Immunofixation electrophoresis showed monoclonal IgG-κ protein
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy findings showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear
key_facts: Patient has a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy
Patient has chronic kidney disease
Patient presented with altered mental status after an unwitnessed fall
New lesions developed on nose, ear, and arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia
Laboratory tests showed acute kidney injury
Peripheral blood smear showed Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate
Serum and urine protein electrophoreses showed abnormal paraprotein band
Immunofixation electrophoresis showed monoclonal IgG-κ protein
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy findings showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions on the face, elbows, knees, and feet, along with laboratory findings of cryoprotein precipitate, abnormal paraprotein band, and elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, is most consistent with cryoglobulinemic purpura, a condition characterized by the deposition of cryoglobulins in blood vessels, leading to purpura and other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: While vasculitis can cause purpuric lesions, the biopsy findings of intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi, without significant vessel wall inflammation, are more suggestive of purpura.

rejected.label: granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The lack of granulomatous inflammation on biopsy and the absence of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: gonorrhea
rejected.why: There is no evidence of gonococcal infection, and the patient's presentation is not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: urticaria
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are described as purpuric macules and patches, rather than the characteristic wheals of urticaria.
